messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: PrIyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: MAP & Eval: Rapid handoff for POC environment (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, peering)

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time today — excited for Cyberleaf to kick off the evaluation. Per our conversation I attached a concise Mutual Action Plan (MAP_RapidHandoff_v1.2.pdf) that isolates the environment checklist we typically complete in week 0 for a short POC. High level items (we can tighten timelines on the call):

- Org setup: tenant creation, admin invite list, and role mappings (Redwood needs one owner + two operators).
- API keys: short-lived API key for trial + optional service account token for dedicated routes.
- IP allowlist: three CIDR ranges for egress and inbound webhook IPs (we'll provide a minimal set; customer provides preferred ranges).
- VPC peering: optional but recommended for sustained throughput testing — peering request, route acceptance, and test VM for validation.
- Acceptance criteria & timeline: 5 business days for environment activation once we have signed MAP and network details.

Action items I need from you to start (by EOD Wed if possible):
1) Confirm tenant owner and two operator emails.
2) Supply IP ranges for allowlist or let us know if you prefer we provide a short list to test first.
3) Procurement contact for contract redlines (we will route the short MAP + SOW).

I've also included a short "network requirements" spreadsheet that lists the minimal firewall rules and sample peering config (cyberleaf-network_requirements.xlsx). If you prefer, we can run a 30-min ramp call Wednesday 10–10:30 PT to run through the items and lock timelines.

Next steps from our side after we receive items above: generate the trial API key, seed the org, and open the peering request.

Thanks,

Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: MAP_RapidHandoff_v1.2.pdf (PDF, 12 pages); cyberleaf-network_requirements.xlsx (XLSX, 2 sheets)

Subject: Re: MAP & Eval: Rapid handoff for POC environment (API keys, org setup, IP allowlist, peering)

Hi Monica — thanks for the clear summary and materials. A few quick clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) Tenant owners: I'll be the owner (alex@cyberleaf.com). Ops: samir.kapoor@cyberleaf.com and elena.cho@cyberleaf.com.
2) IP ranges: We can provide two CIDR blocks for inbound (54.84.0.0/16, 34.216.0.0/16). Are those sufficient for initial testing, or do you require additional egress ranges for the peering path?
3) VPC peering: Security prefers peering only for sustained throughput tests. For the initial week please create the trial keys and we'll defer peering until after functional validation.
4) Procurement: procurement@cyberleaf.com will handle contract redlines — they prefer DocuSign.

We can take the 30-min ramp call on Wednesday 10:00 PT. Please send a calendar invite. Also — any known blockers on ephemeral key rotation we should plan for?

Best,
Alex

Head of Platform Integrations | Cyberleaf Health
alex@cyberleaf.com

Monica / Neha,

Looping internal tech notes and quick checklist for the Wed ramp: I pasted Alex's IP ranges below. A few points we should cover on the call so the customer knows what to expect and who owns what in the MAP: 

- Ephemeral keys: we issue a trial key valid for 72 hours by default for early tests; we can extend to 14 days on request. Rotation endpoint is /v1/keys/rotate and we document the curl snippet in the MAP PDF.
- Org roles: owner privileges required for initial tenant acceptance. After setup we recommend swapping owner to a group admin.
- IP allowlist: initial inbound addresses Alex provided should be fine for webhooks; for outbound egress to model hosting (if they use VPC peering) we'll need the peering ASN and routing table — but that comes later.
- Peering: create a peering draft in our console and send the template for their infra team to fill (I'll prepare).

I'll draft the short peering template and the ephemeral-key snippet into a single one-pager to send post-call.

Priyom
Sr. Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference
